correctness.rationale: Mass-action implies y=(x²+x+r)/(x+2r), with y' strictly positive and full range y>1/2. Twice differentiating pH gives an everywhere-positive factor times P_r(x); exact discriminant -4r³(4r-1)²(112r-1) and Descartes sign count prove all three parameter regimes and exactly two positive zeros only for 0<r<1/112. Exact factorization at equality, Taylor coefficients P_xx=9/28, P_r=1/56, y_x=4 verify critical onset. Strict Jensen and local strict reverse Jensen prove pooling claims. Independently scripted exact rational checks, 3000 finite-difference comparisons and onset tests passed; they are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: Targeted semantic record and scientific literature searches; full readable Deffeyes 1965, Schulz 2009, and Egleston 2010 materials were compared at the level of results. The model equations, conservative mixing, and first-order buffer derivatives are prior results; none of those inspected sources establishes the sharp 1/112 classification of second curvature, double inflection and both signs of equal-alkalinity pH aggregation. Wigley–Plummer 1976 was accessible only as an abstract, leaving priority provisional, not a claim of exhaustive novelty.
residual_risks: Wigley & Plummer 1976 full text was not available for a decisive comparison; claims of full-text noncoverage are not made.
An established generic diprotic-acid curvature or Hessian theorem could imply part or all of this result without matching the same notation.
Fixed total alkalinity in real seawater is not exactly the model’s fixed carbonate alkalinity; this is a scientific scope limitation, not a novelty enhancement.

value.rationale: The model’s two conserved quantities are physically motivated in studies of carbonate-water mixing; evaluating pH before versus after pooling is a concrete mathematical observable. The universal sharp threshold r=1/112, exact full-domain three-band vs one-band classification, and square-root birth of the concave interval identify when the sign of aggregation bias can reverse. This is more informative than first-order buffering or an arbitrary numerical specimen, while remaining explicit about the idealization.
